_meta.purpose: One record per source artefact. independence_group exists so that two sources drawing on the same underlying data are never counted as independent corroboration.
_meta.licence_note: licence describes what we may redistribute. 'cc-by-4.0' permits committing extracted tables with attribution. 'all-rights-reserved' means we cite individual figures under fair quotation but do not commit bulk tables.

denzinger-2001.citation: Denzinger A, Siemers BM, Schaub A, Schnitzler H-U (2001) Echolocation by the barbastelle bat, Barbastella barbastellus. Journal of Comparative Physiology A 187(7):521-528.
denzinger-2001.access_note: Publisher full text is paywalled. Values entered here are taken from the abstract, which is openly available and states them explicitly; abstract text verified via Europe PMC. No table was extracted.

goerlitz-2010.citation: Goerlitz HR, ter Hofstede HM, Zeale MRK, Jones G, Holderied MW (2010) An aerial-hawking bat uses stealth echolocation to counter moth hearing. Current Biology 20(17):1568-1572.
goerlitz-2010.access_note: Values read from the published PDF. Individual figures cited under fair quotation; no bulk table exists in this paper to extract.

collen-2012.citation: Collen A (2012) The evolution of echolocation in bats: a comparative approach. PhD thesis, University College London.
collen-2012.access_note: Not read directly. Recorded because Castro et al. 2024 state their table 3 values were taken from measured data in this thesis (the EchoBank compilation). Present so the derivation chain is explicit and so any future source drawing on EchoBank can be placed in the same independence group.

castro-2024.citation: Castro I, Amado TF, Olalla-Tarraga MA (2024) Correlated evolution between body size and echolocation in bats (order Chiroptera). BMC Ecology and Evolution 24:37.
castro-2024.access_note: Open access. Table 3 of the supplementary docx extracted in full by data/build_castro_calls.py; the docx is cached under data/raw/.

seibert-2015.citation: Seibert A-M, Koblitz JC, Denzinger A, Schnitzler H-U (2015) Bidirectional echolocation in the bat Barbastella barbastellus: different signals of low source level are emitted upward through the nose and downward through the mouth. PLoS ONE 10(9):e0135590.
seibert-2015.access_note: Open access. Table 1 extracted in full with standard deviations.

denzinger-2001-field.notes: Only the abstract was available. Every method field is therefore genuinely unknown rather than merely unrecorded, which is why the durations from this source carry quality_flag=definition_unstated.

castro-2024-unstated.notes: A comparative compilation, not a study with one method: the values are collated from many original sources via Collen 2012, so no single recording or analysis method applies. Every field is therefore genuinely unstated, which is what places these entries at density 'minimal'. Values from this source should lose to any direct measurement with a stated method.

goerlitz-2010-array.notes: Source levels are defined in the text as 'the call amplitude 10 cm away from the bat's mouth' and reported in dB peSPL. Both the 0.1 m reference distance and the peak-equivalent basis are essential: comparing these values directly with rms-at-1-m figures understates the difference by roughly 20 dB of spreading loss plus the peak-to-rms offset.

seibert-2015-array.recorder_model: 16-channel Knowles microphone arrays (4x4 m square and 6 m vertical chain), custom amplifiers, National Instruments acquisition, 16-bit
seibert-2015-array.analysis_software: custom MATLAB scripts; Sonarbeam for beam reconstruction
seibert-2015-array.notes: Reports both apparent source level (assuming the bat is on axis) and absolute source level (corrected for beam direction). Only the absolute value is stored as source_level; the apparent value is recorded in the row notes.
